decisions.reason: The branding change affects the document's brand identity but does not alter the required layout pass, document coverage, formatting, or graphic-treatment coverage.
Changing from GreenLatinos branding to Agua Arc branding does not change the requirement to incorporate photos into the final draft.
The organization chart must still be incorporated into the final draft; the branding decision does not change that action.
The branding shift does not change the requirement to include the budget sheet and supplied proposal tables.
The final deliverable remains a print-ready PDF regardless of whether its visual branding is GreenLatinos or Agua Arc.
The branding decision does not change the Canva source-deliverable format or the client's ability to edit it.
The supplied RFQ narrative content must still be included; changing the visual brand does not alter that content-inclusion requirement.
The branding change does not alter the existing approximate page-count target.

The same message independently establishes the template's modularity and replaceable client credit line, while the Agua Arc brand identity remains owned by the branding Requirement; no template attribute becomes stale.
